OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 25.2 Gross Anatomy of Urine Transport
OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 25.3 Gross Anatomy of the Kidney
OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 25.5 Physiology of Urine Formation

note.text: Your two kidneys sit against the back wall of your belly, just under the ribs. They clean your blood.

steps.title: Ureters
steps.instruction: Trace the tubes from the kidneys down to the bladder.

note.text: Each kidney sends urine down a tube called a ureter. Muscle in its wall squeezes the urine along in waves.
The bladder is a stretchy, muscular bag that collects urine from both ureters and stores it.

steps.title: Urethra
steps.instruction: Draw the tube that carries urine out of the body.

note.text: When the bladder empties, urine leaves the body through the urethra.

steps.title: Inside a kidney
steps.instruction: Trace the enlarged kidney, at the right.

note.text: The outer layer is the cortex. Each kidney holds over a million tiny filters, called nephrons.

steps.title: Medulla
steps.instruction: Trace the four triangles in the middle layer.

note.text: The middle layer, the medulla, is made of cone-shaped pyramids. Tiny ducts in them carry urine inward.

steps.title: Collecting urine
steps.instruction: Trace the funnel and the ureter leaving the kidney.

note.text: Urine drains into a funnel, the renal pelvis, which narrows to become the ureter.

steps.title: Blood in and out
steps.instruction: Draw the two arrows: blood in, then blood out.

note.text: The renal artery brings blood in to be cleaned. The renal vein carries the cleaned blood back toward the heart.

steps.title: Urine's path
steps.instruction: Tap the parts in the order urine passes through them.
steps.why: Kidneys make urine, ureters carry it down, the bladder stores it, and the urethra carries it out.

steps.title: Name the parts
steps.instruction: Pick the name for each numbered part.

mistakes.Urethra: The urethra carries urine out of the body. This tube from the kidney is a ureter.

mistakes.Cortex: The cortex is the outer layer. These triangles are in the middle layer, the medulla.

steps.title: Most comes back
steps.question: Each day the kidneys filter about 180 L of fluid from the blood, but make only 1 to 2 L of urine. Where does the rest go?

options.text: About 99% is taken back into the blood
options.feedback: Yes. The nephrons keep the water and nutrients the body needs and send only wastes and extra water out.
The bladder holds only urine, which is 1 to 2 L a day. The rest returns to the blood.
The lungs breathe out a little water, but the nephrons return almost all the fluid to the blood.
Sweat comes from the skin. The kidneys return almost all the filtered fluid to the blood.

steps.title: Systems working together
steps.question: Which system brings wastes from the body's cells to the kidneys?

options.text: The circulatory system: blood carries the wastes in by the renal artery
options.feedback: Right. Cells dump waste into the blood, and the kidneys clean the blood as it passes through.
Digestive waste leaves through the rectum. Cell wastes travel in the blood.
Nerves carry signals, not wastes. The blood brings wastes to the kidneys.
The lungs remove carbon dioxide. Other wastes travel in the blood to the kidneys.
